title: Sampled burst lab journal — Zara
content:
Purpose:
Personal scratchpad for the stratified/sampled burst experiments I started after the Canary Friday incident. Trying to capture configuration permutations, quick numbers, and hypotheses while they're still fuzzy. This is messy — notes to self and to Ravi/Lena.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- Production observed microbursts that weren't well explained by simple Poisson models; hypothesis is that ingress is a mix of steady baseline + short clustered bursts (multi-request per user) + occasional large waves.
- I want to quantify how different arrival samplers affect tail latency and the effectiveness of KV-prefix caching.

Experiment suite overview (short names):
- strat-sample-v1: stratified arrival with 70/30 baseline/cluster, cluster size drawn from geom(k=2).
- cluster-grid-sweep: sweep cluster size s in [2,4,8,16] with fixed qps.
- asr-smooth: arrival smoothing ratio (ASR) applied to inter-arrival times to emulate client-side rate-limiting.
- kv-prime: prime cache with synthetic hot prefixes vs cold run.

Harness + commands (local bench node -> staging runtime):
- bench-run --pattern=stratified --baseline-qps=800 --clusters-per-min=12 --cluster-size-dist=geom:2 --duration=8m --out=run123.csv
- bench-run --pattern=clustered --cluster-size=8 --burst-rate=2500 --duration=5m --concurrency=600 --out=cluster8.csv
- quick profiling: /opt/redwood/bin/trace-capture --pid=<worker> --span=60s --tags=kvcache,kv-prefetch

Observed aggregate numbers (median of 3 runs each):
(These are rough, use them to prioritize follow-ups)

Config | p50 | p95 | p99 | cold_hit%
------------------------------------------------
baseline (poisson) | 42ms | 120ms | 320ms | 12%
burst-clustered (s=8) | 37ms | 210ms | 740ms | 4%
asr=0.6 (smoothed) | 45ms | 130ms | 360ms | 10%
kv-prime (hot 10%) | 30ms | 95ms | 210ms | 78%

Quick interpretations:
- Clustered bursts reduce median (requests coalesce in batching paths) but massively increase tail — spikes in queueing and head-of-line effects. p99 jumps >2x compared to baseline.
- ASR smoothing (client-side) improves p95/p99 vs raw clustered input, but increases p50 slightly (added spacing reduces batching efficiency). There's a tradeoff.
- KVCaching massively helps tails when hot prefixes are significant; priming 10% of prefixes captured most tail reductions.

Micro-observations / traces:
- In cluster runs, worker logs show periodic short-lived CPU saturation cycles: CPU at 95% for 300-500ms, then back. These align with burst arrivals.
- Trace snapshots show spikes in model kv-cache miss rate during bursts; miss amplification seems to come from concurrent cache population causing eviction thrash.
- One interesting trace: request that hit 3x retries due to transient resource pressure; trace id: b3f6c8 (see linked artifacts).

Open questions / hypotheses to test next:
1) Eviction windows: does increasing async prefetch queue depth reduce miss storms? Test: prefetch-backoff=linear vs exponential.
2) Multi-tenant noise: are bursts tenant-local (single tenant high QPS) or global? Need tenant-tagged ingress runs.
3) Warmup policy: should we implement short-lived micro-warmup (5s) when a burst begins? Prototype: on first request of burst, schedule lightweight kv-prime of top-K prefixes seen in last hour.
4) Quantization interplay: lower-precision kernels reduce CPU time, might mitigate CPU saturation; test cluster-run with q8 model build.

Quick todos (next week):
- [ ] Run cluster-grid-sweep for s in [2,4,8,16] with 5 seeds each and collect full percentiles + p999. (Ravi to help on job orchestration)
- [ ] Add tenant-tagging to bench-run so we can test single-tenant vs multi-tenant bursts. (Lena)
- [ ] Try kvcache LRU-tuning: increase cache size by +20% and instrument eviction-streaks.
- [ ] Capture flame graphs for the 95th-99th percentile windows during a burst.

Notes to self on visualization:
- Heatmap that overlays arrival intensity vs p99 over time is most helpful. Export: runX_timeseries.csv -> quick python seaborn heatmap.
- Use log-scale y-axis for p95/p99 when plotting multiple configs.

Conclusion (short):
- Clustered bursts are a primary driver of tail. KVCaching and client smoothing are effective mitigations but have tradeoffs. Next experiments should focus on eviction/prewarm mechanics and tenant-localization.

Slack refs / tickets:
- #infra-bench: thread 'jan-9 surge postmortem' (see JIRA INF-1842)
- PR with initial bench harness changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/912

Random notes / scraps:
- Observed weirdness: when burst worker CPU hits 100%, grpc conn resets spike; might be epoll backlog exhaustion. Add net.core.somaxconn tweak during test.
- Idea: small adaptive token-budget limiter that drops or delays non-critical requests to preserve p99 for high-priority lanes.

End of dump. Will clean and formalize if any of this looks promising after grid sweep.
